newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB shareholders may sue directors -- paper.
newsitem.headline: DKB shareholders may sue directors -- paper.

text.p: A group of lawyers who own shares in Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd are considering filing a lawsuit against DKB directors over the bank's dubious loans to a firm linked to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday.

The attorneys will first ask auditors of the bank to bring legal action against the directors seeking damages. If no action is forthcoming within 30 days, the lawyers plan to file a representative shareholder suit with the Tokyo District Court, the newspaper said.
The laywers could not immediately be reached for comment on Tuesday morning.
A spokesman for the bank declined to comment on the report, saying it had not heard directly from the laywers about the issue.
The laywers are expected to seek damages totalling 7.5 billion yen, the size of estimated losses on loans extended to the racketeer-linked firm, the newspaper said.
